labels.notes: Read against Maximal_GHD2.tex:544-554 (statement) and 563-581 (proof), the LaTeX itself. (i) Corresponds U psi p q is Def 3.5's condition psi^-1(V' cap psi(U)) cap V != empty, with the boundary memberships dropped. Under T2, mem_frontier_of_corresponds recovers q in the frontier of V, so Lean >= paper. (ii) and (iii): TimelikeCurveIn U gamma a 0 with a < 0 means a future or past chronal curve of U over every closed segment of (a,0). Tendsto over nhdsWithin 0 (Iio 0) is lim_{s->0-}. A smooth timelike curve of U is chronal relative to U, so Lean (ii) quantifies over at least the paper's curves. The reading is disclosed (questions[1]) and is the library convention (Causal/LocateExtension.lean:60). sbierski_prop_3_7_i_imp_ii (elaborated type checked) assumes IsCorrPair, KSide for C, C.dual, D and D.dual with arbitrary S and Sing, D strongly causal and V causally convex. It does not assume p in the frontier of U, q in the frontier of V, convexity of U or a side of a Cauchy surface. Every one of these hypotheses follows from the paper's CGHD setting (U and psi(U) are causally convex GHDs, <= is closed, push-up, strong causality, Sing empty), and the CBG setting supplies them (CGHDData.isCorrPair, kSide_future/_past, causallyConvexIn'). KSide is not a hidden form of (ii). It is a statement about a single spacetime: push-up, causal, closed J+-, K- = I- and Z- at regular points, K- at singular points, density, separation by J+(S), compact J+(S) cap J-(x). It never mentions psi, the other spacetime or curves, and with S empty its S-fields are vacuous. No A3: the import closure has no Causal.CBG.* module, so neither Geometry nor germExt is reachable. Satisfiability is witnessed with a genuine curve on the timelike line (timelikeLine_sbierski_prop_3_7). The equivalence sbierski_prop_3_7 (TFAE, (i)/(ii)/(iii) as above) and sbierski_prop_3_7_unique add C.CausallyArcConnected and p regular. Both are disclosed as strengthened. The label is unmarked and the REPORT status is partial, which is correct. The docstring cites the label without the ** mark (the ledger regex finds no mark), and the ledger row is still 'none'.

counterexample.notes: lightlikeLine_sbierski_prop_3_7_iii_fails is the lightlike line (<< = False), with KSide lightlikeLine {0} univ (every point BTZ), IsCorrPair id on iioOne, strongly causal, causally arc-connected, iioOne causally convex, 1 in the frontier of iioOne and in J+{0}, and Corresponds 1 1. It shows that (iii) fails. Every hypothesis of sbierski_prop_3_7_future holds except hreg, so it is what the REPORT says. It witnesses the regularity hypothesis only: the lightlike line is causally arc-connected. Calling (ii) => (iii) dependent on arc-connectedness in ETT is still fair. The auditor's probe (/tmp, deleted, axioms standard) takes globalLine on R: le as the timelike line, lt U x y := x < y and U = top. It satisfies IsCorrPair id, KSide {0} with Sing empty (p = 1 regular), StronglyCausal, convexity, frontier and J+ membership, and Corresponds 1 1. No TimelikeCurveIn exists in iioOne, and the probe derives not CausallyArcConnected from sbierski_prop_3_7_future itself. So both added hypotheses are needed.

paper_findings.notes: Line 573 and its footnote choose q' in V' cap I^-(p') (resp. W' cap I^-(p')). Line 580 sets q := psi^-1(q'), and the first claim (l.566) only identifies I^-(p') cap psi(U). As written nothing puts q' in psi(U): if V' is large, q' can sit in I^-(p') below psi(U), for example when psi(U) is thin to the past of the Cauchy surface. The repair is one line (shrink V' into I^+(Sigma'), or require q' >> psi(gamma(s0)), then use causal convexity of psi(U) with p' in its closure), so this is an omitted step, not a wrong result. The Lean does exactly this fix: q' in W cap I^-(q) cap I^+(psi(gamma s0)) (SbierskiProp37.lean:257-259), q' in V by Causality.mem_of_le_of_lt_of_mem_closure (:262-263), V causally convex.

'ii) => iii) trivial' needs some timelike curve of U ending at p. In the smooth setting one exists (a past timelike curve from p meets the Cauchy surface inside U, and causal convexity keeps it in U), so 'trivial' is defensible and the REPORT rightly asks only that it be said. The BTZ failure is about ETT's singular extension, and the REPORT says so explicitly.
A remark on proof economy (the WLOG, the t'_i sequence and the interpolant s are not needed), not an error claim. It holds because the kernel-checked proof does not use them.

mark_question: Leaving the label unmarked with status partial is correct. Would a mark be legitimate if the author rules arc-connectedness carried (questions[0])? Only partly. p regular costs nothing in the paper (SingM = SingM' = empty), and the chronal-curve reading (questions[1]) is library convention. But the row 'U a CGHD, psi an isometric embedding -> replaced by IsCorrPair + four KSide + convexity' would still stand. Smooth spacetimes are not in Lean, and kb/0012 says rows that carry model facts as named hypotheses are partial and never marked. So a mark needs the arc-connectedness ruling and also the author's acceptance of that abstraction of the smooth setting, or its layer-3 discharge (smooth-vacuum, T-pkg-smooth-lorentz). It is the author's decision.
